question: A 38-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 1-month history of fatigue and pruritus. Examination of the abdomen shows an enlarged, nontender liver. Serum studies show an alkaline phosphatase level of 140 U/L, aspartate aminotransferase activity of 18 U/L, and alanine aminotransferase activity of 19 U/L. Serum antimitochondrial antibody titers are elevated. A biopsy specimen of this patient's liver is most likely to show which of the following findings?

options.opa: Fibrous, concentric obliteration of small and large bile ducts
options.opb: Intracytoplasmic eosinophilic inclusions in hepatocytes and cellular swelling
options.opc: Macrovesicular fatty infiltration and necrosis of hepatocytes
options.opd: Ballooning degeneration and apoptosis of hepatocytes
options.ope:
Lymphocytic infiltration of portal areas and periductal granulomas
"

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "38-year-old woman with fatigue and pruritus" -> "enlarged, nontender liver on examination" -> "elevated alkaline phosphatase level" -> "elevated serum antimitochondrial antibody titers" -> "suggestive of primary biliary cholangitis" -> "biopsy likely shows lymphocytic infiltration of portal areas and periductal granulomas" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Patient presents with fatigue and pruritus" -> "abdominal examination reveals enlarged liver" -> "serum alkaline phosphatase is elevated" -> "low AST and ALT levels" -> "elevated antimitochondrial antibodies indicate cholestatic liver disease" -> "liver biopsy expected to show lymphocytic infiltration and granulomas" -> 90%

CHAIN: "Symptoms of fatigue and pruritus" -> "nontender enlarged liver found on exam" -> "alkaline phosphatase significantly elevated" -> "low transaminases suggest non-alcoholic fatty liver disease is less likely" -> "elevated antimitochondrial antibodies confirm autoimmune etiology" -> "biopsy findings likely include lymphocytic infiltration and granulomas" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Fatigue and pruritus in a 38-year-old woman" -> "nontender liver enlargement noted" -> "alkaline phosphatase level is high" -> "low AST and ALT suggest minimal hepatocellular injury" -> "positive antimitochondrial antibodies indicate primary biliary cholangitis" -> "biopsy findings expected to show lymphocytic infiltration and periductal granulomas" -> 90%
analysis: The patient's symptoms of fatigue and pruritus, along with the elevated alkaline phosphatase level and positive antimitochondrial antibodies, suggest primary biliary cholangitis (PBC). In PBC, liver biopsy typically shows lymphocytic infiltration of portal areas and periductal granulomas, which is characteristic of this autoimmune condition affecting the bile ducts.
